# Ontology reference

Generated from [`ontology/seamline.yaml`](../../ontology/seamline.yaml), version 1.0.0, core profile, v0.1. The vocabulary is licensed CC-BY-4.0. The normative source is the YAML; this page is a rendering of it and is checked against it on every `pnpm verify`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Node kinds | 29 |
| Edge kinds | 26 |
| Domain/range pairs | 54 |
| Extractors with a manifest | 5 |

Kind names are identity tokens: the same spelling is used in the YAML, in `packages/ontology/src/contract.ts`, in serialized output and in queries. The agreement between the YAML and the contract is enforced by `ontology/lint.mjs` (`pnpm gate:ontology`).

## Node kinds

"Produced by" lists the extractors whose manifest claims authority for the kind in `produces`. A kind with no producer is one no extractor manifest claims; the host may still write it (it writes `Alias` nodes on every extraction, and it keeps runs and extractor results in their own store tables, `runs` and `extractor_results`, rather than as `Run` or `Extractor` nodes). An extractor may also emit a kind as an edge endpoint without claiming it (`extract-change` emits `File` that way), which is not listed.

### Change

| Kind | Profile | Default sensitivity | Natural key | Produced by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Changeset` | core | internal | `(repo, changeset_id)` | `extract-change` | A working diff or a set of commits under review. What blast radius is computed for. |
| `Commit` | core | internal | `(repo, sha)` | `extract-change` | A git commit. Its message is third-party-authored text and is tagged untrusted. |

### Code

| Kind | Profile | Default sensitivity | Natural key | Produced by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CodeField` | core | internal | `(repo, canonical_qualified_name, field_name)` | `extract-code-ts` | A field or property declared on a symbol. One of the four endpoints of the field-level cross-domain join that is this project's wedge. |
| `File` | core | internal | `(repo, posix_path)` | `extract-code-ts` | A source file, addressed by repo-relative POSIX path. |
| `Module` | core | internal | `(repo, module_specifier)` | `extract-code-ts` | A module or package: an importable unit, which is not always one file. Module -> File containment is enumerated explicitly, because the predecessor design declared containment as all-domains and consequently had no module-to-file edge at all while four of its views traversed one. |
| `Parameter` | core | internal | `(repo, canonical_qualified_name, ordinal)` | `extract-code-ts` | A parameter of a function or method. |
| `Repo` | core | internal | `(repo)` | `extract-code-ts` | A source repository. The namespace component of every node id. |
| `RouteHandler` | core | internal | `(repo, http_method, path_template)` | `extract-code-ts`, `extract-contracts` | An HTTP route as the code exposes it: method plus path template. Distinct from Operation, which is the route as a contract DECLARES it. Keeping them separate is what makes contract drift detectable at all. |
| `Symbol` | core | internal | `(repo, canonical_qualified_name)` | `extract-code-ts` | A declared symbol: class, interface, type alias, enum, function, or method. One kind with a symbol_kind property, not six kinds, because six would multiply every edge signature touching a symbol by six and buy nothing. Identity: resolved through re-exports and barrels to the DECLARATION site by the type checker. Resolving to the import site would make identity depend on which file was scanned first, which is a path dependency wearing a different name. |

### Meta

| Kind | Profile | Default sensitivity | Natural key | Produced by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Alias` | core | internal | `(repo, former_canonical_name)` | none declared | A rename mapping. When a canonical name changes, an ALIAS_OF row records old to new and history survives the rename. Identity is path-free for every kind except File, so a git mv changes no other id, unless it changes an input that the id is built from; a File's canonical name is its repo-relative path, so for a File that git reports as renamed the Alias is how history follows it. See docs/adr/ADR-0016, which lists those inputs. |
| `Contradiction` | core | internal | `(repo, code, left_id, right_id)` | none declared | Two authoritative facts that disagree, citing both facts and the join path along which they were compared. A NODE referencing two facts, never an edge between edges: the predecessor design required three edges that put edges and types in node positions, which no property-graph store supports. |
| `Extractor` | core | internal | `(extractor_name, version)` | none declared | An extractor and its capability manifest, including the provenance ceiling the host enforces. An extractor may not assert a provenance above its ceiling; infer-join therefore cannot emit EXTRACTED, and that is a runtime error rather than a code-review question. |
| `Lens` | core | internal | `(repo, lens_name)` | none declared | A named saved view over the graph. |
| `Run` | core | internal | `(repo, run_id)` | none declared | One extraction. Carries started_at and finished_at, which is the ONLY place wall-clock time appears. Every node and edge lifecycle field is a run id rather than a timestamp, which is what makes byte-identical output achievable. |
| `ThreatModel` | core | restricted | `(repo, threat_model_id)` | none declared | A recorded threat model. Defaults to restricted. Seamline is its own first user: THREATMODEL.md is a Phase-0 deliverable, because a verification tool that does not model its own threats is making a claim it has not tested on itself. |

### Kinds with no edges

These kinds are the source or target of no edge in the core profile. Each carries a recorded reason in the YAML (`seamline_unreachable_waiver`).

- `Contradiction`: No edge, by design. A contradiction references its two facts through the left and right node-id FIELDS on the record, not through graph edges. Making them edges would be reification (an edge whose endpoints are themselves facts about edges), which is the construct v3 removed. This waiver is the de-reification decision, recorded where it can be seen.
- `Lens`: No edge in v0.1. All 24 predecessor lenses are deferred behind a named consumer, and the CLI prints lineage and contradictions as human-readable text, or as JSON with --json, instead (CSV and Mermaid output are not implemented). The predecessor design's PROJECTS edge (Lens -> kinds) is exactly the reification v3 removed, so when lenses land their kind selection will be a property, not an edge. The kind is reserved so a later lens implementation is additive rather than breaking.
- `TestRun`: No edge in v0.1. TestRun is the authoritative-evidence anchor the deferred needs matrix requires: a rule at error severity must cite a TestRun result at the commit plus coverage intersecting the realizing symbols, never a substring in a test name. The TestCase -> TestRun result edge lands with the needs matrix, behind a named consumer. Reserving the kind now costs nothing; adding a node kind later is an ontology-breaking change.
- `ThreatModel`: No edge in v0.1. The kind exists so that the security spine has a place in the vocabulary from commit one rather than being retrofitted, and so Seamline can record its own threat model in its own graph. Edges from ThreatModel to the assets and controls it covers require the infrastructure and control kinds, which are deferred.

## Edge kinds

Every edge declares its domain and range as an enumerated list of (source, target) pairs; "any to any" is not allowed. Edge identity is `UNIQUE(scope, src, dst, kind)`. Only `infer-join` declares its edge kinds in its manifest (as the selector of its `produces` claim), so for every other edge the "Produced by" column reads "none declared": the other extractors do not state their edges in a machine-readable form.

### Change

| Edge | Profile | Domain to range | Produced by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RENAMED_FROM` | core | `File` to `File`; `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | Rename detection from git similarity plus content hashes. Note the limit honestly: git rename detection is a heuristic, so a rename combined with a heavy edit can fall below the threshold and be recorded as delete-plus-create. The graph stays correct; the history across that rename is what is lost. |
| `TOUCHES` | core | `Changeset` to `Symbol`; `Commit` to `File`; `Commit` to `Symbol` | none declared | A commit or changeset touches a file or symbol. The input to blast radius. |

### Code

| Edge | Profile | Domain to range | Produced by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CALLS` | core | `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | A symbol calls another symbol, resolved by the type checker. |
| `DECORATED_WITH` | core | `CodeField` to `Symbol`; `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | A symbol or field carries a decorator. Decorators are how most ORM and validation frameworks declare the facts the join needs. |
| `EXPORTS` | core | `File` to `Symbol`; `Module` to `Symbol` | none declared | A file or module exports a symbol. Barrel re-exports are deduplicated by construction during resolution, and the resolved target is always the declaration site. |
| `EXTENDS` | core | `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | Class or interface inheritance. Edges resolved through an interface or an abstract base carry reduced confidence, because the call target is not determined by the declaration alone. |
| `HANDLES_ROUTE` | core | `Symbol` to `RouteHandler` | none declared | A symbol handles an HTTP route as the code exposes it. |
| `IMPLEMENTS` | core | `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | A class implements an interface. |
| `IMPORTS` | core | `File` to `File`; `Module` to `Module` | none declared | One file or module imports another. |
| `QUERIES` | core | `Symbol` to `Table` | none declared | A symbol reads or writes a table. The bridge from the code layer to the data layer, and the traced write path several detectors depend on. |
| `USES_TYPE` | core | `CodeField` to `Symbol`; `Parameter` to `Symbol`; `Symbol` to `Symbol` | none declared | A symbol, field, or parameter references a type. One of the inputs to type-disagreement detection. |

### Containment

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CONTAINS` | core | `Contract` to `Operation`; `Contract` to `SchemaProperty`; `DataSource` to `Schema`; `Entity` to `DomainProperty`; `File` to `Symbol`; `Module` to `File`; `Repo` to `File`; `Repo` to `Module`; `Schema` to `Table`; `Symbol` to `CodeField`; `Symbol` to `Parameter`; `Table` to `Column` | none declared | Structural containment. Twelve enumerated pairs, spanning code, data, contract, and domain. Never all-domains. |

| `IMPLEMENTED_BY` | core | `Operation` to `RouteHandler` | none declared | A declared operation is implemented by a route handler. Its ABSENCE in either direction is contract drift, and that finding is legitimate precisely because both endpoints are extracted facts rather than annotations. |

|---|---|---|---|---|

The edge that turns a database column into an API surface, and therefore the edge that makes PII-reachable-without-auth answerable. |

| Edge | Profile | Domain to range | Produced by | Description |

| `COVERS` | core | `CoverageRecord` to `File`; `CoverageRecord` to `Symbol` | none declared | A coverage record intersects a symbol or file. |
| `TESTS` | core | `TestCase` to `Symbol` | none declared | A test case exercises a symbol. EXTRACTED from what the test imports and calls. It is deliberately not derivable from a substring in a test name: the predecessor design's verification gate was satisfied by naming a test after a requirement, which asserts that a link exists rather than that anything was verified. |

## Fields carried by every node and edge

Field names are written as in the YAML (snake_case); the TypeScript contract uses camelCase (`first_seen_run` is `firstSeenRun`) and the mapping is mechanical. `created_at` and `updated_at` are deliberately absent: byte-identical output is a release gate, and time belongs to the run, not to the fact.

### Node fields

| Field | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | `string` | Natural key, `{repo}:{kind}:{canonicalName}`, path-free for every kind except File, whose canonical name is its repo-relative path. Deliberately not a synthetic UUID or ULID: an id minted at first sight is not stable across a rebuild-from-scratch, and rebuild-from-scratch is the operation this design rests on. See docs/adr/ADR-0002, and docs/adr/ADR-0016 for the File exception and for the inputs through which a move or rename changes another id. |
| `kind` | yes | `string` | The node or edge kind. Pinned per class by slot_usage, so a class and its kind cannot disagree. |
| `name` | yes | `string` | Display name. Not identity. |
| `path` | no | `string` | Repo-relative POSIX path. A PROPERTY, part of identity only for File (whose canonical name it is), and never absolute. Stored because the re-run invalidation rule needs it and because determinism forbids absolute paths. |
| `profile` | yes | `ProfileEnum` | Which profile this kind belongs to. Class-level metadata, pinned per class with `equals_string` rather than carried per instance, which is why there is no corresponding runtime field on SeamlineNode in contract.ts. See docs/adr/ADR-0001. |
| `sensitivity` | yes | `SensitivityEnum` | Export classification. Required on every node and defaulted per kind, so a new kind cannot be added without a sensitivity decision. |
| `provenance` | yes | `ProvenanceEnum` | Where this fact came from. Merge resolves conflicts by the total precedence order, then by (extractor_priority, run_id), so the winner does not depend on input order. |
| `confidence` | yes | `float` | Calibrated confidence in [0,1]. Ranks within a provenance level; it never substitutes for one. |
| `source_ref` | no | `string` | Pointer to the authoritative source this was read from. |
| `untrusted` | no | `boolean` | True when any string field derives from third-party content: dependency metadata, issue and pull-request text, commit messages, code comments. Such text is delimited when rendered into agent context, so that an attacker who lands a comment in a transitive dependency cannot issue instructions to a reading agent. See docs/adr/ADR-0006. |
| `props` | no | `string` | Open key/value map of kind-specific scalar properties. Values are string, number, boolean, or null. Sorted by key before serialization. |
| `first_seen_run` | yes | `string` | Run id in which this was first observed. Replaces created_at: run granularity, no wall clock. |
| `last_seen_run` | yes | `string` | Run id in which this was most recently observed. |
| `deleted_at` | no | `string` | Tombstone marker. Set when the fact vanished from an authoritative scope of a PASSing run; CLEARED on re-insert, so a fact that reappears is resurrected rather than shadowed by a second row. Never hard-delete. See docs/adr/ADR-0003. |

### Kind-specific properties

Kind-specific values live in the open `props` map (string, number, boolean or null values, sorted by key before serialization). The ontology does not declare per-kind property keys, so none are listed here. The property names the contradiction detectors read, and the extractors that emit them, are documented per code in [docs/contradictions](../contradictions/README.md).

## Enumerations

### ContradictionCodeEnum

The v0.1 contradiction catalogue. Each detector compares two authoritative facts and never the absence of a declaration. See docs/adr/ADR-0005.

- [`X10_UNTESTED_PII_WRITE`](../contradictions/X10.md): A symbol writes a pii column and no TESTS or COVERS intersects it.
- [`X1_NULLABILITY`](../contradictions/X1.md): Column.nullable disagrees with the SchemaProperty.required or CodeField optionality it is joined to.
- [`X2_TYPE`](../contradictions/X2.md): Column.type, CodeField.type, and SchemaProperty.type disagree across a join.
- [`X3_CONSTRAINT`](../contradictions/X3.md): Column length or check constraint disagrees with the validator enforcing it.
- [`X4_UNBACKED_PROPERTY`](../contradictions/X4.md): A response SchemaProperty has no BACKED_BY column and no computing symbol.
- [`X5_UNWRITTEN_COLUMN`](../contradictions/X5.md): A NOT NULL column with no default is never written by any traced write path.
- [`X6_PII_UNAUTHENTICATED`](../contradictions/X6.md): A column with pii is reachable from an Operation with no declared auth.
- [`X7_VALIDATOR_DIVERGENCE`](../contradictions/X7.md): A validator enforces a constraint the database does not, or the reverse.
- [`X8_ORPHANED_MIGRATION`](../contradictions/X8.md): A Migration references a Table or Column that no longer exists.
- [`X9_CONTRACT_DRIFT`](../contradictions/X9.md): An Operation has no IMPLEMENTED_BY route handler, or a handler implements no declared operation.

### ExtractorStatusEnum

Per-extractor outcome for a run. UNAVAILABLE is never PASS. See docs/adr/ADR-0003.

- `FAIL`: Ran and errored. Tombstones nothing; queries over its scope return UNKNOWN.
- `PASS`: Ran to completion and is authoritative for its declared scope.
- `UNAVAILABLE`: Could not run at all: input absent, tool missing, credentials absent. Tombstones nothing. Never treated as a clean result, because a clean result and an absent extractor are indistinguishable from their output alone.

Every node kind in the core profile. Must equal NODE_KINDS in contract.ts, and must equal the set of classes deriving from SeamlineNode.

### ProfileEnum

Which profile a kind belongs to. See docs/adr/ADR-0001.

- `core`: Shipped and live. v0.1 extractors emit core kinds only.
- `extended`: Reserved vocabulary. Inert: no extractor produces it, no detector reads it, no query traverses it. It exists to reserve the name.
- `vendor`: Reserved for third-party extensions. Never produced by a first-party extractor.

### ProvenanceEnum

Where a fact came from. Total precedence order, highest first: EXTRACTED > DECLARED > INFERRED > LLM_SUGGESTED. See docs/adr/ADR-0007.

- `DECLARED`: Asserted by a human, typically as an annotation, and reviewed.
- `EXTRACTED`: Read directly from an authoritative source by a first-party extractor. Outranks a human annotation deliberately: an annotation that disagrees with the compiler is wrong.
- `INFERRED`: Derived by name, type, or structure matching. Stored in the insert-only annotations table; never mutates a fact; never feeds a gate.
- `LLM_SUGGESTED`: Proposed by a model. Lowest precedence. Promotion to DECLARED writes a new row retaining prov:wasAttributedTo; attribution is never overwritten.

### SensitivityEnum

Export classification, defaulted per kind and required on every node. Export is default-deny: a profile is an allow-list and there is no export-everything flag. See docs/adr/ADR-0006.

- `confidential`: Restricted to those who need it. Data-layer kinds default here: a schema is a map of where the data lives.
- `internal`: Safe within the organization.
- `public`: Safe to publish.
- `restricted`: Highest classification. People and threat models default here.

### SeverityEnum

Severity of a contradiction.

- `critical`
- `high`
- `low`
- `medium`

## Extractor manifests

What each extractor declares in its capability manifest. `provenanceCeiling` is the highest provenance the host lets it emit; a claim names a scope, the node kinds the extractor is authoritative for in that scope, and a selector bounding the claim.

| Extractor | Provenance ceiling | Scope | Node kinds | Selector |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extract-change` | EXTRACTED | `change` | `Changeset`, `Commit` | `HEAD max=500` |
